briefs.headline: Miami (Ohio) scores 34 unanswered to beat Ohio 34-17 and end a 6-game winning streak
briefs.summary: The Ohio Bobcats led 17-0 at Yager Stadium in Oxford with 7:20 left in the second quarter on Nick Poulos' 8-yard touchdown pass to Riley Neer, Duncan Brune's 1-yard run and Brack Peacock's 22-yard field goal, and did not score again: true freshman Drew Bellisari, in his first college game after Caleb Heavner was hurt late in the half, went 8 of 15 for 99 yards and ran three times for 64, Miami (Ohio) cut it to 17-7 at the break on receiver Scoop Smith's 15-yard throw to Maleek Huggins, D'Shawntae Jones scored from a yard out in the third, and Brady Stidham's 36-yard field goal 44 seconds into the fourth and 25-yarder with 3:55 left put the RedHawks ahead. Poulos then fumbled on fourth down, Jones ran 48 yards on the next play, and Amariyun Knighten returned Poulos' first interception of the season 58 yards; Poulos finished 20 of 39 for 193 yards and ran for 68, Ohio was 3 of 17 on third down, and the Bobcats are 7-3 and 5-1 in the MAC, level with Western Michigan and no longer the league's only unbeaten team in conference play, with Toledo at 4-1; Ball State visits Peden Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 7 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Ohio State beat Marshall 84-74 in Columbus after a 14-0 Herd run closed it to 7
briefs.summary: Noah Otshudi scored 27 points on 12-of-18 shooting and Bryce Slay 15 for the Marshall Thundering Herd on Monday night at the Schottenstein Center, in a game that was not reported in Tuesday's paper; Ohio State's Jimmie Williams scored five points in a 12-0 run to 22-9, the Buckeyes led 45-27 at halftime and by as many as 19 in the second half, and Marshall scored 14 straight to get within 77-70 on Slay's two free throws with two minutes left before going empty on its next three possessions. Marshall shot 5 of 22 from 3 and had seven assists to 15 turnovers, Ohio State made 25 of 35 free throws to Marshall's 11 of 15, and the Buckeyes have not lost to a Sun Belt team since 1998; the Herd are 1-2 and play at Youngstown State on Saturday at 6 p.m. ET, the same hour the football team kicks off at home against App State.

briefs.headline: Manchester United open talks with Pochettino's representatives, ESPN reports; Carrick still takes training
briefs.summary: ESPN reported Wednesday morning, citing sources, that Manchester United are in contact with U.S. men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino and have opened talks with his representatives, that he is the leading candidate to replace Michael Carrick, and that the 54-year-old, who signed a new U.S. Soccer contract in August, is keen on the job; Carrick led Tuesday's session at Carrington and is set to take training again Wednesday while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco, where club sources told ESPN no final decision has been taken and any change needs sign-off from Ratcliffe and the Glazers. ESPN named Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Kieran McKenna and Fabian Hurzeler as others considered; the USMNT plays Haiti in the first leg of a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal on Saturday in Miami at 4:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Bengals back out of an agreed Ebiketie trade after finding it would cost a compensatory 3rd-round pick
briefs.summary: The Bengals pulled out of a deal to acquire Philadelphia edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie for a sixth-round pick on Tuesday, ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported, citing sources, after it emerged that signing a player on a one-year free-agent contract would have cost Cincinnati the 2027 compensatory third-round pick OverTheCap.com projects it to receive, largely for losing Trey Hendrickson to Baltimore in free agency; the Bengals were looking for an edge rusher after rookie Cashius Howell, with a sack, five quarterback hits and a 15.3% pressure rate in seven games, went on injured reserve with a right wrist injury from Week 8. Ebiketie has a 4.6% pressure rate and two quarterback hits in nine games; the 4 p.m. ET deadline passed with the Bengals making no trade, and ESPN's Ben Solak listed them among the deadline's losers. Pittsburgh visits Paycor Stadium on Sunday night at 8:20 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Simons, ahead of schedule on his ACL, is set to rejoin Tottenham training after the break
briefs.summary: Xavi Simons, 23, who tore an anterior cruciate ligament in Tottenham's one-goal win at Wolves on April 25 and missed the World Cup, is set to enter the third phase of his rehabilitation later in November and return to team training after the international break, seven months after the injury, PA reported Tuesday, which would put a competitive return before the nine-month mark at the end of January within reach; speaking at the Oxford Union on Oct. 30, Simons said he watched the rest of last season's relegation fight from a hospital bed, that he had bad moments at night his family did not know about, and that he is putting in endless hours. Tottenham, 11th on 12 points, next host Ipswich on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 10 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Van Dijk says there is no panic over a Liverpool contract that runs out in June
briefs.summary: Virgil van Dijk, 35, who has played every Premier League minute for Liverpool this season on the two-year extension he signed in April 2024, said Tuesday that he is not in any panic about a deal that expires next summer, that there is nothing to report, that he wants to keep playing and that if it is not extended he will go somewhere else; he has withdrawn from the Netherlands' Nations League matches against Greece and Germany after carrying a knock, and called the club's progress under Andoni Iraola a work in progress still looking for consistency. It follows Alisson's Monday remarks about talks over his own expiring contract; Liverpool, 4th on 18 points, host Manchester United on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 11:30 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Ura pushes out Hoshoryu for his first kinboshi in 25 tournaments; the yokozuna has lost 2 straight
briefs.summary: Maegashira (rank-and-file) 2 Ura, 34, pushed out yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu in the final bout of day 4 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center on Wednesday, the second straight day Hoshoryu has given up a kinboshi (gold star, a rank-and-filer's win over a yokozuna) after Fujiryoga's on day 3: Hoshoryu opened with two-handed thrusts and then pulled back, and Ura, who had lost his first three bouts to Kirishima, Atamifuji and Aonishiki, followed him out for his first win. It is Ura's third career kinboshi and his first since beating Terunofuji at the 2022 Aki basho, 25 tournaments ago, after Harumafuji at Nagoya in 2017, and makes three different yokozuna he has beaten; Hoshoryu had won 10 of their 16 previous meetings. Ura said he was happy and had resolved to try his hardest; Hoshoryu, 27, back after three tournaments out following right knee surgery, has two wins and two losses, and Japan Sumo Association chairman Hakkaku had said before the bout that the yokozuna's legs were not yet fully right and that he needed to return to the mindset of day 1. Ura meets yokozuna Onosato in Thursday's final bout.

briefs.headline: Atamifuji is the lone unbeaten after 4 days as Aonishiki falls to Fujiryoga and the other ozeki win
briefs.summary: Sekiwake Atamifuji, 24, at 198 kilograms the heaviest man in the top division, forced out new komusubi Mitonoumi after being taken to the edge, and became the sole leader on day 4 when the three maegashira who had won their first three bouts, Dewanoryu, Takanosho and Kinbozan, all lost; Asakayama, the former ozeki (champion) Kaio, said from ringside that Atamifuji is watching his opponent and attacking forward, and added that it would be good if it continued, a reference to the five straight losses that left him at eight wins and seven losses at the Aki basho after an ozeki run. Yokozuna Onosato, chasing a second straight yusho (championship), threw maegashira 2 Fujiseiun by sukuinage (beltless arm throw) for a third straight win; ozeki Kotozakura forced out Asanoyama and ozeki Kirishima drove out Takayasu from behind, both with three wins and a loss; ozeki Aonishiki was thrown by uwatenage (overarm throw) by maegashira 1 Fujiryoga, who has now beaten a yokozuna and two ozeki in four days, and has two wins and two losses; and sekiwake Fujinokawa, 21, thrust down komusubi Yoshinofuji for his first win after three losses. Atamifuji and Fujinokawa meet in a sekiwake bout Thursday. Atamifuji is not giving interviews during the tournament, Sponichi reported, a message passed through an attendant.

briefs.headline: Vikings reacquire Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 3rd-round pick; Mendoza starts in Las Vegas
briefs.summary: Minnesota traded a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas for Kirk Cousins, 38, on Tuesday, less than 24 hours after Carson Wentz went 8 of 25 for 81 yards with three turnovers in Monday night's loss at Buffalo while Kyler Murray sat with a Grade 2 hamstring strain; Raiders general manager John Spytek said talks did not materialize until Tuesday, that the team was not actively shopping Cousins, and that the conversation with him was not the easiest. Cousins, who threw 20 touchdown passes in nine starts for Las Vegas, second in the NFL, played for the Vikings from 2018 to 2023 and for coach Kevin O'Connell in 2022 and 2023; Minnesota, with six wins and two losses, released Odell Beckham Jr. to make room and owes Cousins the rest of a $1.3 million base salary and a $10 million roster bonus in the spring, and 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza takes over as the Raiders' starter at home against Seattle this week.

briefs.headline: Colts trade Downs to the Chiefs and Allen to the 49ers but keep Taylor and Jones as the deadline passes
briefs.summary: Indianapolis sent Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick to Kansas City for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks and Keenan Allen, 34, to San Francisco for a 2027 sixth-rounder before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline, the Chiefs having gone since Week 4 without a Patrick Mahomes completion of more than 20 air yards and the 49ers having played without Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr., Demarcus Robinson, De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk at various points; running back Jonathan Taylor, for whom the Colts sought a first-round pick and the Giants offered a second and a fifth before withdrawing, and quarterback Daniel Jones were not moved. Elsewhere, Denver got linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Chargers, Buffalo safety Amani Hooker from Tennessee, and Baltimore center Ryan Neuzil from Atlanta for guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick, per ESPN's tracker.

briefs.headline: George scores 36 in his return to Philadelphia as the Celtics beat the 76ers 123-101
briefs.summary: Paul George made 6 of 11 3-pointers and scored 14 straight points in the fourth quarter against the team that traded him for Jaylen Brown, and said afterward that he had rolled a middle finger at a fan who dropped a loose ball at his feet; Jayson Tatum scored 21 in his first game against Brown since the trade, and Brown, who did not acknowledge Tatum's pregame approach at midcourt, had 13 points, four turnovers, a game-worst minus-27 and two first-quarter fouls, his first multiple-foul first quarter of the season, and said it was a tough night and that he was frustrated. Boston has nine wins and two losses and leads the East by half a game over Philadelphia, with nine and three; the 76ers' LeBron James shook Tatum's hand in the exchange Brown walked past.

briefs.headline: Lillard's 25 lead the Trail Blazers past the short-handed Thunder 123-103
briefs.summary: Damian Lillard scored 25, hitting back-to-back 3-pointers to turn a two-point deficit into a 79 to 71 lead and one from the logo for a 17-point lead entering the fourth, Deni Avdija had 24 points and eight assists and Sidy Cissoko 17 starting for Scoot Henderson as Portland, with seven wins and three losses, ended a two-game slide; Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 26 on 8-of-22 shooting, missed all four 3s and sat the fourth quarter for Oklahoma City, now with eight wins and three losses, which was without Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams and had won four straight. The teams play again in Portland on Wednesday; in New York, Jalen Brunson's 23 and Karl-Anthony Towns' 21 points and 16 rebounds carried the Knicks past Milwaukee 117-85, the Bucks' seventh straight loss, leaving them with one win in 11 games.

briefs.headline: Georgia takes the CFP committee's No. 1 spot, Utah is No. 2 and Notre Dame climbs to 5th
briefs.summary: The College Football Playoff selection committee's second rankings on Tuesday put Georgia, with eight wins and one loss, first, unbeaten Utah second, two-loss Alabama third and unbeaten UCLA fourth, with Notre Dame up six places to 5th after beating Miami, which fell six to 7th; Texas is 6th, Tennessee 8th, Indiana 9th after an open date, BYU 10th, Kentucky 11th and Texas Tech 12th, though No. 24 Boise State would take the 12th seed as the fifth conference champion if the bracket were set today, giving first-round games of Boise State at Notre Dame, Kentucky at Texas, BYU at Miami and Indiana at Tennessee. Committee chair Hunter Yurachek said Alabama is first in both record strength and schedule strength; Ohio State dropped eight places to 20th, Houston is 14th and Arizona 24th. The final rankings come Dec. 6, with first-round games Dec. 18 and 19.

briefs.headline: Kaprizov's power-play goal 21 seconds into overtime beats the Canadiens 2-1 on Price's night
briefs.summary: Kirill Kaprizov's 17th goal, a one-timer on a power play that began when Cole Caufield was called for slashing with 56 seconds left in regulation, gave Minnesota (13-3-4) a 2-1 win in Montreal after Carey Price, inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday, received an ovation of nearly four minutes at his ring-of-honor ceremony; Bobby Brink scored on a third-period breakaway after a Josh Anderson turnover, Nick Suzuki tied it with 1:38 left with the goalie pulled, and Jesper Wallstedt made 27 saves to Jacob Fowler's 22. Montreal (11-3-4) is 8-0-3 in its last 11; in Winnipeg, Dawson Mercer and Kyle Connor scored twice each as the Jets beat New Jersey 4-2 on the night Connor Hellebuyck, who did not dress, was booed through warmups in his first return since the Oct. 23 trade.

briefs.headline: Murphy wins a 3rd straight NL Manager of the Year from a hospital bed; Venable takes the AL award
briefs.summary: Pat Murphy, 67, who led Milwaukee to a franchise-record 103 wins and its first World Series title, became the first manager to win the award in three consecutive seasons since it began in 1983, taking 20 of 30 first-place votes and 124 points to Atlanta's Walt Weiss (seven, 86) and Philadelphia's Don Mattingly (one, 25), and accepted it on MLB Network after hip replacement surgery; Will Venable of the White Sox, two years removed from a 121-loss season, won the American League award with 15 first-place votes and 111 points to Kevin Cash's 12 and 98. Separately, Bob Boone, the seven-time Gold Glove catcher on the Phillies' 1980 champions who managed the Reds for three seasons and the Royals for three, died Tuesday at 78, his son Bret said; no cause was given.

prime.item: Day 5 of 9. The duck table's second segment opened Saturday, Nov. 7, and closes Sunday, Nov. 15, four days out, with the third segment Dec. 21 through Jan. 31; the first, Oct. 3 to 11, is closed, and both youth waterfowl days, Sept. 19 and Oct. 31, are past. The migratory summary's duck line reads daily bag six, possession 18, with the sub-limits in footnote (c): no more than four mallards, two of them hens, two black ducks, three pintails, three wood ducks, two redheads, two canvasbacks and four sea ducks, no more than three scoters and three long-tailed ducks among them; scaup, inside the duck bag, reads one per day Nov. 7 to 15 and Dec. 21 to Jan. 11 and two per day Jan. 12 to 31; coots run the same dates as ducks at 15 and 45, mergansers the same dates at five and 15 in aggregate. Canada and white-fronted geese and snow and blue geese share the Nov. 7 to 15 segment and a third Dec. 8 through Jan. 31, daily bag five and possession 15 in aggregate; brant open Jan. 2 at one and three. Shooting hours for waterfowl are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and HIP registration is required. The dates are not in the hunting and trapping pamphlet, which says so itself; they were re-read this morning from WVDNR's separate Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary 2026-2027, which fetched through the proxy at 5:45 a.m. (HTTP 200, 1,940,942 bytes, md5 aad32d21343547146e3977a821a39355, byte-identical to Tuesday's copy, a 26th straight morning).

The migratory summary's line reads daily bag 15, possession 45, and its shooting-hours paragraph puts dove hours at one-half hour before sunrise to sunset for every day but the first segment's opener. The dates are not in the hunting and trapping pamphlet, which says so itself; they were re-read this morning from WVDNR's separate Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary 2026-2027, which fetched through the proxy at 5:45 a.m. (HTTP 200, 1,940,942 bytes, md5 aad32d21343547146e3977a821a39355, byte-identical to Tuesday's copy, a 26th straight morning).

waters.reading: 43.1 cfs, 1.24 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on flow against 48.8 cfs and steady on stage against 1.29 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Against Tuesday's edition reading of 45.3 cfs and 1.26 feet at 5:15 a.m. the gauge is down 2.2 cfs and 0.02 feet on the day, and the recession took one more step and a half: the USGS record held 45.3 from Monday night to 6:45 a.m. Tuesday, dropped to 44.2 and traded the two values through the middle of the afternoon, held 44.2 from 4:45 p.m., reached 43.1 at 1:15 a.m. Wednesday with one 15-minute return to 44.2, and has read 43.1 since 2 a.m.; the stage went 1.26, 1.25, 1.24 on the same steps. The fetcher's 24-hour comparison figures, 48.8 and 1.29, are Monday morning's values, a 48-hour window, so the day's true change is the 2.2 cfs above. At 43.1 the Williams is at the lowest reading of the fall for a fourth straight morning, under Tuesday's 45.3, Monday's 48.8 and Sunday's 52.4, on a slide this paper has recorded from 1,360 cfs on Oct. 15 through 653 on Oct. 17, 141 on Oct. 24 and 70.7 on Oct. 31. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, printed as it stands, "43 cfs - prime wading water." Stocking: WVDNR's trout-stocking page answered this morning's fetch with a redirect to a notice about Bear Rock Lakes WMA and no stocking list, so no stocking line runs; the river's most recent stocking this paper has reported is Oct. 29. At 43 cfs and clear the Williams is the file's low-water problem, a notch lower again: pocket water and plunge pools shrunk to their cores, every fish in the deepest slot of each pocket, the water cold and glass-clear, and a wading angler the loudest thing on the river. Structure is pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks; forage is caddis, stoneflies and sculpin. So: a long leader, nine to 12 feet to 6X or 7X, and small flies, a size 16 to 18 caddis pupa or a size 18 soft-hackle swung into the plunge-pool tailouts, a size 16 to 18 pheasant tail or small black stonefly nymph under a tiny indicator or a dry-dropper through the pocket seams, a size 20 to 22 blue-winged olive on top through the warmest part of the afternoon, and for the one bigger fish in each plunge pool a size 8 to 10 olive or black sculpin pattern fished on a short line into the foam at the head of the pool at first or last light, before the sun gets on it; an egg pattern or a San Juan worm under a small indicator still covers the holdover stocked pools. The heavy-nymph-on-the-seam game is for 500 cfs, a number this river has not seen since the 653 of Oct. 17.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.02 feet at 5 a.m., rising against 24.74 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.0 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Tuesday's edition reading of 25.32 at 5 a.m. the pool is down 0.30 on the day, and the day was a round trip the other way from Monday's: the trace fell from 25.32 at 5 a.m. Tuesday through 25.03 at 7:30, 24.79 at 9:30, 24.62 at 12:30 p.m. and 24.52 at 2:30 to a low of 24.47 at 4:30 p.m., then turned up through 24.69 at 5, 24.81 at 8:15, 24.93 at 9, 25.00 at 12:30 a.m. Wednesday and 25.05 at 3:15 a.m., and read 25.02 at 5 a.m. The Williams fell all day, and neither trace says rain; the pool drained through Tuesday's daylight and refilled overnight, the same shape as Monday evening's rise, and whether that is the dam's overnight holding pattern or water from upstream the gauge does not say and this paper will not guess. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, 25.0 feet and rising, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 25.0 the gauge is two feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27. A pool in normal band that moved six-tenths down and back in a day fishes the structure, not the slack: wing dams, riprap and the lock wall are the file's structure, shad and skipjack with crawfish in the rock the forage. A white or pearl three-and-a-half to four-inch swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of each wing dam at first light for hybrids and white bass; a crawfish-colored jig or a three-inch tube dragged slow on the riprap through the middle of the day for smallmouth and drum; and with the water cooling through November a half-ounce blade bait or a jig and minnow worked vertical along the lock wall seam and the barge-cut edges for sauger, cut skipjack on the bottom in the cuts after dark for blue catfish. A pool that is refilling at first light puts bait on the inside edges of the wing dams and the flooded rock through the morning, so the first hour goes to the inside edges rather than the current faces, and the afternoon drain, if it repeats, pulls the fish back to the faces.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.03 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.21 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.0 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Against Tuesday's edition reading of 26.22 at 5 a.m. the gauge is down 0.19 on the day, with the same afternoon dip and overnight recovery as Monday: the trace topped at 26.36 at 6 a.m. Tuesday, held between 26.15 and 26.32 through the morning, fell from 26.09 at 1 p.m. through 25.90 at 4 and 25.81 at 8:30 to a low of 25.69 at 10:15 p.m., then climbed through 25.91 at 1 a.m., 25.96 at 2:45 and 26.07 at 4:45 a.m. to 26.03 at 5 a.m. Wednesday. The dam below tells most of it again: the USGS gauge at Ironton, Ohio, below Greenup Dam, recorded Greenup's discharge climbing from 24,000 cfs at 5 a.m. Tuesday to 32,800 at 8 a.m., where the record pauses until 1:30 p.m., then falling through 26,500 at 2 p.m., 18,400 at 4 and 14,000 at 5:30 to 9,610 at 7 p.m., and recovering through 13,500 at 9, 17,900 at 11:45 and 21,500 at 1 a.m. to 25,100 at 5 a.m. Wednesday; the Ironton stage ran from 34.59 at 5:15 a.m. Tuesday down to 33.97 at 9:30 p.m. and back to 34.28 at 4:45 a.m. So Greenup throttled back through Tuesday afternoon and evening and the Huntington reach dropped two-thirds of a foot with the Ironton pool, then both came back overnight as the dam passed more water, while the Byrd pool above did the same thing on its own schedule; the two gauges are within a foot of each other again this morning, and neither trace says rain. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. Below the dam the reach is back near Tuesday morning's level with Greenup drawing 25,100 cfs below, which is push on the seams, and the fishing goes to them: a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of the wing dams at first light for hybrids and white bass, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head worked slow along the lock wall's downstream edge for sauger, a crawfish jig on the riprap at midday, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the slack beside the discharge after dark for blue and flathead catfish. No color in either trace; the slack-behind-the-dams game is for a muddy river, not this one.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 3:02 AM at 0.4 ft, high 9:13 AM at 4.1 ft, low 3:50 PM at 0.7 ft, high 9:27 PM at 3.1 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 1:37 AM at 0.4 ft, high 8:15 AM at 5.3 ft, low 2:45 PM at 0.6 ft, high 8:32 PM at 3.7 ft. Water 66.2F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon waxing crescent, 3% illuminated, 1.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 9:13 AM and 9:27 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All four of the sound's events land inside the calendar day, the 3:02 a.m. low behind us at press time, and so do the surf's, the 1:37 a.m. low at Ocean City Beach pier having come an hour and 25 minutes ahead of the sound's; the sound lags the surf 58 minutes on the morning high, 65 on the midday low and 55 on the evening high, the long-lag-on-the-ebb pattern the reference describes. The whole table is 39 to 42 minutes later than Tuesday's, and the ranges have come off the top of the cycle by a tenth or two: a 3.7-foot fill overnight from 0.4 to this morning's 4.1, a tenth under Tuesday's 4.2, a 3.4-foot drain to 3:50 p.m., a 2.4-foot fill to the 9:27 p.m. high, which at 3.1 is two-tenths under Tuesday's evening high, and the surf's 5.3 morning high is a tenth under Tuesday's 5.4. The moon is a day and a half past new, a 3% waxing crescent, so these are still spring tides and the inlet still runs hard either side of slack, easing a little each day toward the first-quarter neap next week. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, reads 66.2F, up 0.7 on Tuesday's 65.5 and the first morning-to-morning rise since Saturday's 68.2; NOAA's hourly record at Beaufort ran from 65.5 at 5 a.m. Tuesday to 66.9 at 8 p.m. before easing back overnight. What's running: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report for November, published Sunday, Nov. 1, is 10 days old this morning, a monthly report and not today's conditions. It has the Jolly Roger Pier starting to see scattered speckled trout, with night bottom fishing producing good-sized Virginia mullet and spot and bluefish thick in the early mornings; Surf City Pier with pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom, casting shots at Spanish and bluefish, and king mackerel very good before the last blow; East Coast Sports with the piers catching a few big red drum of 32 inches and more, mostly on the north end, smaller reds and occasional trout inside, and trout to dominate as it cools; Native Son with the wind pushing bait around, the five- to eight-foot seams of the creeks the depth to work for trout, cut bait the best red drum bait, and false albacore possible off the beach; Capt. Ricky Kellum with many smaller specks and some to 28 inches on live shrimp under a cork in four to eight feet of water most often, 3/16-ounce jigheads for the artificials, and black drum to 18 inches and smaller reds on the same floated shrimp over structure; Carolina Flats with topwater early to find the trout schools, deeper holes later, and reds in a last blitz on the oyster and grass banks on soft plastics before the bait thins; and the boats with kings on slow-trolled bait in 50 to 60 feet, bluefish, false albacore and gray trout on nearshore structure, and sea bass, snapper and triggerfish on the bottom in 60 to 80 feet. Beach conditions: no NWS product was active for coastal Pender or Onslow, the Topsail point or the adjacent marine zones at 5:45 a.m., and the NWS active-alerts feed for North Carolina was empty. Tide is the whole game, and this morning it is the last two hours of the flood at press time: the sound fills to 4.1 at 9:13 a.m. and then drains for six hours and 37 minutes to the 3:50 p.m. low, a long morning-into-afternoon ebb. Structure here is oyster bars, grass edges, dock lights and the ICWW channel, forage mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet, which is the report's live-shrimp-and-small-plastic fishing. Trout first: a topwater plug over the flooded grass edges in the first hour of light, with the water still coming in toward the 9:13 a.m. high, then a 3/16- or quarter-ounce jighead with a paddletail or soft jerkbait worked slow down the five- to eight-foot seams where the creek channels drop into the ICWW as the drain gathers through late morning and midday, and a popping cork with live shrimp over the oyster bars on the first of the flood after 4 p.m. and again either side of the 9:27 p.m. high; with the water at Beaufort in the mid-60s the trout hold the deeper holes on the afternoon low. Red drum want the last of the fall, which on this table is roughly 1:15 to the 3:50 p.m. low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges as the grass drains; the dusk high at 9:27 p.m. puts drum up on the flooded grass and oyster banks for a weedless gold spoon or a soft plastic, and the ebb that follows runs under the dock lights toward Thursday's pre-dawn low, the report's small plastics or a suspending twitchbait where the shrimp and finger mullet stack. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel an hour either side of the evening high. Bluefish are the early-morning fish on the beach behind the bait pods on a metal jig or topwater, per both piers. Flounder are release only.
